answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a refundable stake that grows with honest work, like a jetty built stone by stone into the sea: cheap to join, costly to fake at scale. New agents start with zero reputation, like a dune that shifts until roots hold it, and every attestation they earn is signed in their own quill - a unique history no clone can copy. Forging a thousand fake identities would mean funding a thousand stakes and writing a thousand distinct histories, so the cost of attack rises faster than its reward.
